chunks: Sahl, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Al-Hakam ibn Miskin, from Jameel ibn Darraj, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Where is this strike to be applied?' meaning the one who has sexual relations with a Mahram (close relative). He (peace be upon him) said: 'His neck is struck,' or he said: 'His throat.'

key_terms.ذَاتَ مَحْرَمٍ: A close relative with whom marriage is prohibited

ai.seo_question: Where is the strike applied for someone who commits incest with a Mahram?
ai.summary: In this concise narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific anatomical target for the execution of a person guilty of incest (*Zawil Mahram*), specifying the neck (*raqabah*) or throat. This detail highlights the precision of Shia jurisprudence in applying the death penalty, distinguishing it from general execution methods by focusing on the vital area to ensure immediate fatality. The term *raqabah* here refers to the neck as the site of the fatal blow, underscoring the severity of the sin due to the violation of close kinship ties.
